references.text: Moses and Joshua stand before God, and leaders are appointed over the people, similar to the appointment of military commanders in Deuteronomy 20:9.
One man from each tribe shall stand by their side, as head of his family's house - this concerns the appointment of leaders over Israel's army.
Organization of Israel's camp with leaders at the head of each division, reflecting military organization with commanders.
Joshua orders the people's overseers to go through the camp and prepare the people - overseers who convey commands to the people in a military context.
Samuel describes how the king will appoint leaders over thousands and over fifties, showing military organization with commanders.
Saul organizes the army with thousand-leaders, demonstrating the practice of appointing military leaders at the head of the people.
David musters the army and sets leaders over thousands and over hundreds - this is a direct parallel to the appointment of commanders.
